summary: People wrongly told a woman her husband died overseas, so she remarried. When her first husband comes back, she must leave both men and loses many rights. Other Tannaim give some of the rules differently.

chunks.en: A woman whose husband went overseas,
chunks.st: With regard to a woman whose husband went overseas, and witnesses

chunks.en: and people came and told her,
chunks.st: came and they said to her:

chunks.en: "Your husband died,"
chunks.st: Your husband is dead,

chunks.en: and she married someone else, and then her husband came back,
chunks.st: and she married another man on the basis of this testimony, and afterward her husband came back from out of the country,

chunks.en: she must leave both of them,
chunks.st: she must leave both this man and that one, as they are both forbidden to her.

chunks.en: and she needs a get from both of them.
chunks.st: And she requires a bill of divorce from this one and that one.

chunks.en: She gets no kesubah, no payment for fruits,
chunks.st: And furthermore, she has a claim to neither payment of her marriage contract, nor the profits of her property used by either of them,

chunks.en: no food, and no worn-out things,
chunks.st: nor sustenance, nor the worn clothes she brought to the marriage.

chunks.he: לֹא עַל זֶה וְלֹא עַל זֶה.
chunks.en: not from this one and not from that one.
chunks.st: She has rights to these claims neither against this man nor against that one, i.e., she cannot collect these payments from either her first or second husband.

chunks.en: If she took them from either one,
chunks.st: And if she took any of these items from this man or from that one, she must

chunks.en: she must give them back. And the child is a mamzer from either one.
chunks.st: return them to him. And the offspring is a mamzer from this one and from that one.
chunks.stMore: Her child from the second husband is a definite mamzer, as she was never divorced from her first husband, and the Sages decreed that if she returned to her first husband, a child born later from him is also a mamzer.

chunks.en: Neither of them may become tamei for her if she dies,
chunks.explain: A Kohen may become tamei to bury his wife, but not here.
chunks.st: And neither this man nor that man may become impure for her upon her death, if they are priests.

chunks.en: and neither of them gets
chunks.st: And neither this one nor that one is entitled to the rights that stem from the marriage bond:

chunks.en: the things she finds, or what she earns,
chunks.st: Neither to her found articles, nor to her earnings,

chunks.en: or the right to cancel her nedarim.
chunks.st: nor to the nullification of her vows. If she

chunks.en: If she was a Jewish woman,
chunks.st: was a regular Israelite woman,

chunks.en: she becomes unfit to marry a Kohen;
chunks.st: she is disqualified from marrying into the priesthood, as her intercourse with the second husband is considered an act of illicit sexual relations,

chunks.en: a Levi's daughter becomes unfit to eat ma'aser,
chunks.st: and the daughter of a Levite is disqualified from partaking of the first tithe,

chunks.en: and a Kohen's daughter unfit to eat terumah.
chunks.st: and the daughter of a priest is disqualified from partaking of teruma.

chunks.en: And the heirs of this one and the heirs
chunks.st: And neither the heirs of this man nor the heirs of

chunks.en: of that one do not inherit her kesubah.
chunks.st: that one inherit her marriage contract, as she is not considered married to either of them. This clause will be explained in the Gemara.

chunks.en: And if they died,
chunks.st: And if they both died childless,

chunks.en: the brothers of this one and the brothers of
chunks.st: the brothers of this one and the brothers of this one

chunks.en: that one do chalitzah, but not yibum.
chunks.st: must perform ḥalitza and they do not enter into levirate marriage.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosi says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei disagrees with the first tanna and says that she does receive payment of her marriage contract, and the obligation of

chunks.en: her kesubah is paid from her first husband's property.
chunks.st: her marriage contract is upon the property of her first husband.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar says:

chunks.en: The first one gets what she finds and what she earns,
chunks.st: The first husband is entitled to her found articles, to her earnings,

chunks.en: and may cancel her nedarim.
chunks.st: and to the nullification of her vows. Since her second marriage was an error, the first husband does not forfeit his rights.

chunks.en: And Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says an even more far-reaching ruling:

chunks.en: her yibum or chalitzah with the brother
chunks.st: Her sexual relations or her ḥalitza with the brothers

chunks.en: of the first husband frees her co-wife,
chunks.st: of the first husband exempts her rival wife, as it is considered a proper levirate marriage or ḥalitza, and certainly she does not require ḥalitza from the brother of the second husband.

chunks.en: and a child from him is not a mamzer.
chunks.st: And if she returns to her first husband, the child from him is not a mamzer. All these halakhot refer to a situation when she married with the permission of the court, after hearing that her husband had died.

chunks.en: And if she married without permission,
chunks.st: But if she married without the consent of the court, basing herself entirely on the testimony she heard, and her husband returned, it is

chunks.en: she may go back to him.
chunks.st: permitted for her to return to her first husband.

summary: If she remarried because beis din allowed it, she does not need to bring a korban. If she remarried on her own, she must bring one.

chunks.en: If she married by permission of beis din,
chunks.st: The mishna adds another difference between these two scenarios: If she married by permission of the court,

chunks.en: she must leave, but she does not bring a korban.
chunks.st: she must leave both of them and she is exempt from bringing the offering, i.e., the sin-offering for her unwitting adultery, as she had the authorization of the court and is therefore considered to have acted under duress. If, however, she

chunks.he: לֹא נִסֵּת עַל פִּי בֵית דִּין,
chunks.en: If she did not marry by permission of beis din,
chunks.st: did not marry by permission of the court,

chunks.en: she must leave, and she must bring a korban.
chunks.st: she must leave her second husband and is liable to bring an offering for mistakenly having relations with a man forbidden to her.

chunks.en: The power of beis din is great,
chunks.st: In this regard, the power of the court is greater,

chunks.en: since it frees her from the korban.
chunks.st: as she is exempt from bringing an offering. If the

chunks.en: If beis din told her she may marry,
chunks.st: court instructed her to marry on the basis of inaccurate testimony,

chunks.en: and she went and did wrong,
chunks.st: and she went and ruined herself by engaging in licentious relations outside matrimony,

chunks.en: she must bring a korban,
chunks.st: she is liable to bring an offering,

chunks.en: because they only allowed her to marry.
chunks.st: as they permitted her only to marry, and not to engage in licentious relations.

summary: Wrong reports about whether her husband or her son died first can change whether she needed yibum. If the report was wrong, her marriage was forbidden and she must leave.

chunks.he: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁהָלַךְ בַּעֲלָהּ וּבְנָהּ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם,
chunks.en: A woman whose husband and son went overseas,
chunks.st: With regard to a woman whose husband and child went overseas, and witnesses

chunks.en: and people came and told her,
chunks.st: came and said to her:

chunks.he: מֵת בַּעְלֵךְ וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵת בְּנֵךְ,
chunks.en: "Your husband died, and after that your son died,"
chunks.explain: Then she had a child when her husband died, so no yibum was needed.
chunks.st: Your husband died and afterward your child died, she does not require levirate marriage, as she had a child when her husband died.

chunks.en: and she married. Then they told her,
chunks.st: And for this reason she married another man. And if afterward they said to her that

chunks.en: "It was the other way around,"
chunks.st: the matters were reversed, i.e., the child died before the husband, which means that she did require levirate marriage, she is therefore a yevama who married a stranger without ḥalitza and

chunks.en: she must leave, and the first and last children are mamzerim.
chunks.st: she must consequently leave her second husband. And with regard to the first child, the one born before they heard about the reversal, and the last one, born after they realized who actually died first, each of these children is a mamzer.

chunks.en: If they told her,
chunks.st: Conversely, if they said to her:

chunks.he: מֵת בְּנֵךְ וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵת בַּעְלֵךְ,
chunks.en: "Your son died, and after that your husband died,"
chunks.st: Your child died and afterward your husband died,

chunks.en: and she did yibum, and then they told her,
chunks.st: and she therefore entered into levirate marriage, and afterward they said to her that

chunks.en: "It was the other way around,"
chunks.st: the matters were reversed, which means she married her husband’s brother when there was no obligation of levirate marriage,

chunks.en: she must leave, and the first and last children are mamzerim.
chunks.st: she must leave her husband, and the first child and the last one are each a mamzer.

chunks.en: If they told her,
chunks.st: If they said to her:

chunks.en: "Your husband died,"
chunks.st: Your husband died,

chunks.en: and she married, and then they told her,
chunks.st: and she married, and afterward they said to her that

chunks.en: "He was alive then, and died later,"
chunks.st: he was alive at the time of her marriage and he later died,

chunks.en: she must leave, and the first child is a mamzer,
chunks.st: she must leave the second husband. And the first child, born when her original husband was still alive, is a mamzer,

chunks.en: but the last one is not a mamzer.
chunks.st: and the last one, born after his death, is not a mamzer.

chunks.en: If they told her,
chunks.st: If they said to her:

chunks.en: "Your husband died,"
chunks.st: Your husband died,

chunks.en: and she got engaged, and then her husband came back,
chunks.st: and she became betrothed to another man, and afterward her husband came,

chunks.en: she may go back to him.
chunks.st: she is permitted to return to him, as betrothal alone does not render her forbidden to her husband.

chunks.en: Even though
chunks.st: Furthermore, although the

chunks.en: the second man gave her a get,
chunks.st: last man, i.e., her betrothed, gave her a bill of divorce,

chunks.en: he did not make her unfit to marry a Kohen.
chunks.st: he has not thereby disqualified her from marrying into the priesthood.
chunks.stMore: She was never his wife, for the betrothal was invalid, and a bill of divorce given to the wife of another man does not disqualify her.

chunks.en: This is what Rabbi
chunks.st: This was taught by Rabbi

chunks.en: Elazar ben Masya explained:
chunks.st: Elazar ben Matya: The verse states with regard to priests: “

chunks.en: "A woman divorced from her husband" (Vayikra 21),
chunks.st: Neither shall they take a woman divorced from her husband” (Leviticus 21:7), which indicates:

chunks.en: and not from a man who is not her husband.
chunks.st: And not one who was divorced from a man who is not her husband, e.g., the second man in this case.

summary: A man was wrongly told that his wife died, and he married her sister. When his wife comes back, she may return to him. The mishnah also tells which children are mamzerim.

chunks.en: A man whose wife went overseas,
chunks.st: In the case of one whose wife went overseas and people

chunks.en: and people came and told him,
chunks.st: came and told him:

chunks.en: "Your wife died,"
chunks.st: Your wife is dead,

chunks.en: and he married her sister,
chunks.st: and he married her sister,

chunks.en: and then his wife came back,
chunks.st: and afterward his wife came back from overseas, the original wife

chunks.en: she may go back to him.
chunks.st: is permitted to return to him, as his erroneous marriage to her sister is considered licentious sexual relations, and one who has intercourse with his wife’s relatives has not rendered his first wife forbidden to himself.

chunks.en: He is allowed to the second one's relatives,
chunks.st: And he is permitted to the relatives of the second woman, e.g., her daughter,

chunks.en: and the second is allowed to his relatives.
chunks.st: and this second woman is permitted to his relatives, e.g., his son, as the marriage was entirely invalid.

chunks.en: And if the first one died,
chunks.st: And if the first woman died he is

chunks.en: he may marry the second.
chunks.st: permitted to the second woman, despite the fact that he has already engaged in forbidden relations with her. If

chunks.en: If they told him,
chunks.st: they said to him

chunks.en: "Your wife died,"
chunks.st: that his wife is dead,

chunks.en: and he married her sister,
chunks.st: and he married her sister, and

chunks.en: and then they told him,
chunks.st: afterward they said to him that

chunks.en: "She was alive then,
chunks.st: she was alive when he married the sister

chunks.en: and died later," the first child is a mamzer,
chunks.st: and only later died, in this case the first child, born to the sister while his wife was still alive, is a mamzer, as he was born from the union of a man and his sister-in-law,

chunks.en: and the last one is not a mamzer.
chunks.st: and the last one is not a mamzer.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosi says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: Whoever makes unfit through others
chunks.st: Whoever disqualifies others

chunks.en: makes unfit through himself,
chunks.st: also disqualifies himself,

chunks.he: וְכָל שֶׁאֵין פּוֹסֵל עַל יְדֵי אֲחֵרִים,
chunks.en: and whoever does not make unfit through others
chunks.st: and whoever does not disqualify others

chunks.en: does not make unfit through himself.
chunks.st: does not disqualify himself either. Rabbi Yosei’s obscure statement will be explained by the Gemara.

summary: A man was told again and again that his wife died, and each time he married her sister. When they all turn out to be alive, only some of the marriages count. The mishnah tells which ones.

chunks.en: They told him,
chunks.st: Witnesses said to a husband:

chunks.en: "Your wife died,"
chunks.st: Your wife is dead,

chunks.en: and he married her sister from her father.
chunks.st: and he married her paternal sister, and witnesses subsequently told him that his second wife

chunks.en: She died, and he married her sister from her mother.
chunks.st: was dead and he married her maternal sister; afterward witnesses said that this one too

chunks.en: She died, and he married her sister from her father.
chunks.st: was dead and he married her paternal sister;

chunks.en: She died, and he married her sister from her mother.
chunks.st: finally they told him that she was dead and he married the last woman’s maternal sister,

chunks.en: And they all turned out to be alive.
chunks.st: and then they were all discovered to be alive.

chunks.en: He is allowed to the first,
chunks.st: In this case he is permitted to his first wife,

chunks.en: the third, and the fifth,
chunks.explain: These are not sisters of each other, so these marriages count.
chunks.st: and to the third and to the fifth. Since these women are not sisters, his betrothal to them is effective. Consequently, if he died

chunks.en: and they free their co-wives,
chunks.st: and one of them entered into levirate marriage, they exempt their rival wives.

chunks.en: and he is forbidden to the second and the fourth,
chunks.st: But he is forbidden to the second and fourth wife, each of whom is the sister of his original wife. Therefore, if he passed away and the yavam had relations with one of them, his

chunks.he: וְאֵין בִּיאַת אַחַת מֵהֶן פּוֹטֶרֶת צָרָתָהּ.
chunks.en: and yibum with one of them does not free her co-wife.
chunks.st: relations with any one of them does not exempt her rival wife, as she was forbidden to his brother, which means there was no mitzva of levirate marriage here at all.

chunks.en: And if he married the second
chunks.st: And if he had relations with the second woman in the aforementioned list

chunks.en: after the first one really died,
chunks.st: after the death of the first, i.e., the first one indeed died but the other rumors were all false, in that case he is

chunks.en: he is allowed to the second and the fourth,
chunks.st: permitted to the second and the fourth, who are his lawful wives,

chunks.en: and they free their co-wives,
chunks.st: and they exempt their rival wives,

chunks.en: and he is forbidden to the third and the fifth,
chunks.st: and he is forbidden to the third and the fifth, the sisters of the women married to him,

chunks.he: וְאֵין בִּיאַת אַחַת מֵהֶן פּוֹטֶרֶת צָרָתָהּ:
chunks.en: and yibum with one of them does not free her co-wife.
chunks.st: and the sexual relations of the brother with any one of them does not exempt her rival wife.

summary: A boy nine years and one day old who does yibum is not like a grown-up, but what he does still counts in some ways. His brothers' acts can block him even if they come later.

chunks.en: A boy nine years and one day old
chunks.st: The mishna addresses a different issue: If a boy aged nine years and one day had relations with his yevama

chunks.en: makes her unfit for the brothers,
chunks.st: he thereby disqualifies his brothers from levirate marriage, despite the fact that as a minor he has not acquired the yevama through this act of intercourse,

chunks.en: and the brothers make her unfit for him.
chunks.st: and the brothers likewise disqualify the woman from him if they have intercourse with the yevama.

chunks.en: But he makes unfit only if he is first,
chunks.st: However, there is a difference between them, as he disqualifies them only if he engaged in relations with her first,

chunks.en: and the brothers make unfit whether first or last.
chunks.st: and the brothers disqualify him whether they had relations first or last. The mishna explains:

chunks.en: How so? A boy nine years and one
chunks.st: How so? A boy

chunks.en: day old who did yibum with his yevamah
chunks.st: aged nine years and one day who had relations with his yevama

chunks.en: made her unfit for the brothers.
chunks.st: has disqualified his brothers, as they are no longer eligible to marry her.

chunks.en: If the brothers did yibum with her,
chunks.st: If his brothers had relations with her,

chunks.en: or made a maamar with her,
chunks.st: or performed levirate betrothal with her,

chunks.en: or gave a get, or did chalitzah,
chunks.st: or gave her a bill of divorce, or performed ḥalitza with her,

chunks.en: they made her unfit for him.
chunks.st: they permanently disqualify him from engaging in relations with her.

summary: If two young brothers, each nine years and one day old, both did yibum with the same widow, the second one makes her unfit for the first. Rabbi Shimon disagrees.

chunks.en: A boy nine years and one

chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says he does

summary: A boy nine years and one day old who did yibum with one widow and then with her co-wife makes them unfit for himself. Rabbi Shimon disagrees. If he dies, his yevamah does chalitzah, and a wife he married is free.

chunks.en: A boy nine years and one
chunks.st: If a minor aged nine years and one day

chunks.en: day old who did yibum with his yevamah,
chunks.st: had relations with his yevama, and afterward that same boy

chunks.en: and after that with her co-wife,
chunks.st: had relations with her rival wife, he thereby

chunks.en: made them unfit for himself.
chunks.st: disqualifies her to himself, and both women are now forbidden to him.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says he does

chunks.explain: A young boy's marriage does not count from the Torah.
chunks.st: she is exempt from levirate marriage and ḥalitza, as by Torah law a minor cannot marry.

summary: A boy did yibum when he was nine, and when he grew up he married another woman and died. The first widow does only chalitzah, but the second may do yibum. The same is true for an older man who still has not shown signs of growing up.

chunks.en: A boy nine years and one
chunks.st: If a boy aged nine years and one day

chunks.en: day old who did yibum with his yevamah,
chunks.st: had relations with his yevama,

chunks.en: and after he grew up he married another woman and died.
chunks.st: and after he matured he married a different woman and then died childless,

chunks.he: אִם לֹא יָדַע אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה מִשֶּׁהִגְדִּיל,
chunks.en: If he did not live with the first one after he grew up,
chunks.st: if he did not carnally know the first woman after he matured, but only when he was a minor,

chunks.en: the first does chalitzah, but not yibum,
chunks.st: the first one performs ḥalitza and may not enter into levirate marriage, as she is in essence a yevama who had relations with a minor,

chunks.en: and the second either does chalitzah or yibum.
chunks.st: and the second woman either performs ḥalitza or enters into levirate marriage, as she is his full-fledged wife.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says: The brother

chunks.en: He does yibum with whichever he wants,
chunks.st: consummates levirate marriage with whichever woman he chooses,

chunks.en: and does chalitzah with the other.
chunks.st: and performs ḥalitza with the second one.

chunks.en: The same is true for one who is nine
chunks.st: The mishna comments: This is the halakha both for a boy who is nine

chunks.en: years and one day old,
chunks.st: years and one day old,

chunks.en: and for one who is twenty years old
chunks.st: and also for one who is twenty years old

chunks.en: who has not shown two hairs.
chunks.explain: Two hairs are a sign of growing up.
chunks.st: who has not developed two pubic hairs. He has the status of a nine-year-old boy in this regard, as his intercourse is not considered a proper act of intercourse.
